How search works

This page uses a small local index of Xenors content. It does not need a separate search server. The query in the address bar is used only to filter the local list, while the canonical URL remains the clean search page. This means older search URLs can land on a real page instead of a 404.

Search tips for technical questions

Use the smallest useful phrase first. A query such as “Python functions” or “CSS grid” usually finds a better tutorial match than a long sentence. Once you open a page, use its table of contents to jump to examples, common mistakes or exercises.

If you are learning a subject from the beginning, search can get you to an answer quickly but a structured track is usually faster overall. The Code Lab tracks are ordered so later lessons can reuse concepts introduced earlier.

When your query is an error message, remove machine-specific paths, tokens and IDs before searching. Keep the important exception name and the part of the message that describes the failure. Then compare the result with the smallest reproducible example in your own code.

For current AI or technology features, include the product name and year only when freshness matters. For stable programming concepts, the underlying topic matters more than the year in the query.
